subject: Compensation anchors and geo-tiering: proposal & next steps
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 12 Jul 2027 09:03:00 -0700
Subject: Initial comp-anchor proposal and geo-tiering framing

Team —

Following up from last week's calibration sync: attached is comp-band-proposal-v2.xlsx and the raw market extract (market-data-2027.csv). High-level framing below — please skim, we should lock decisions by end of week if we want to reflect in next hiring cycle.

Key proposals:
- Move to three anchor points per level (Lower Anchor, Mid Anchor, Upper Anchor) instead of two to reduce border-case escalations.
- Geo-tiering: collapse current 8 micro-zones into 3 primary tiers (Tier A: high-cost metros; Tier B: mid-cost metros; Tier C: non-metro/remote). Multipliers are in column "Geo Multiplier" in the sheet.
- Introduce a small experience adder for ICs at L4+ for demonstrated delivery (up to +5% but not automatic).

Questions I want input on:
1) Are the Tier A multipliers too aggressive for our budget targets?
2) Do we want to retain any country-level overrides (APAC/LATAM exceptions)?
3) Approval flow: should director-level approval suffice for offers inside band, or do we require People Ops sign-off for >10% variance?

I've annotated rows where I used external benchmarking from HireBench and TalentMetrics (source credited in the CSV).

Thanks,
Karthik

--
Karthik Iyer
Director, Total Rewards
Redwood Inference

From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 12 Jul 2027 11:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Initial comp-anchor proposal and geo-tiering framing

Karthik —

Nice work pulling the data together. A few quick thoughts after a first pass:

- Tiering: I support the 3-tier collapse — it simplifies recruiter guidance and should speed offers. My only ask is to make the mapping decision (which cities fall into Tier A vs B) explicit in the sheet — right now a handful of borderline metros aren't assigned.

- Anchor spacing: three anchors is the right direction but the Upper Anchor in L6 looks out of step with market top-quartile; recommend a modest compression (Upper -> Upper -4%). See comments in the "L6" row.

- Approval flow: propose the following: Director sign-off for within-band up to +7%; People Ops sign-off for >+7% and any out-of-band offers; Executive approval for >+20% or special equity exceptions. This keeps day-to-day velocity and protects us on large deviations.

Action items for this thread:
1) Karthik: mark the ambiguous metros in the sheet and add a short mapping tab.
2) Marissa: would you run a quick headcount forecast for Q4 offers under the new tier multipliers? We want to flag budget delta before rollout.
3) Hannah: can you flag any regulatory or payroll constraints for country-level overrides (if we keep them)?

I'll prep a one-pager for the People leadership review assuming we land these decisions.

Best,
Laura

--
Laura Bennett
VP, People Operations
Redwood Inference

From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 13 Jul 2027 08:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Initial comp-anchor proposal and geo-tiering framing

Laura/Karthik —

Quick regulatory note: if we implement country-level overrides for APAC, payroll vendors will require separate mapping for statutory benefits and may add a small per-offer processing fee for manual exceptions. For LATAM we should be cautious about multi-currency posting; recommend we centralize posting in USD with local currency conversions in the offer packet to avoid payroll tax misfires.

I also did a first pass on the Tier A candidate list and marked Seattle and Boston as Tier A, put Denver and Austin in Tier B pending headcount risk review. See the comments in the attached draft mapping in the spreadsheet.

One other ask: can we add a short guidance blurb for hiring managers in the sheet explaining when to seek people ops early (complex offers, retention risk, relocation)? That will reduce last-minute escalations.

Thanks,
Hannah

--
Hannah Schmitt
Senior Manager, Talent Acquisition
Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 13 Jul 2027 10:00:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Initial comp-anchor proposal and geo-tiering framing

Folks —

Thanks for the notes. I ran three hiring scenarios through the quarter model with the proposed multipliers (low/expected/high hire volume). Key takeaways:

- Net incremental comp budget (expected scenario): +4.6% headcount cost vs current bands, driven mostly by raising mid-anchor for L4-L6 and the Tier A multipliers.
- Topline risk: if hiring skews heavily to Tier A metros (30%+ new hires) we could see up to +8.2% uplift; we should monitor requisition locations closely.
- Headcount approvals: recommend we cap offer flexibility for L4-L5 to +10% without CFO notification; L6+ exceptions should trigger Finance review.

Attached: geo-tiering-summary.pdf (one-pager for leadership), and updated comp-band-proposal-v2.xlsx with city mappings and my scenario tabs.

Proposed next steps (quick cadence):
1) Karthik: finalize mapping tab and compress L6 upper anchor by 4% as Laura suggested.
2) Hannah: add hiring manager guidance snippet to the sheet.
3) Laura/People: prepare the one-pager for Thursday's leadership POP (People Ops) review.
4) We will record budget delta and route to Finance if headcount mix shifts to >25% Tier A hires.

If there's alignment on this, I'll post the final one-pager and ask for sign-off in the leadership channel.

Cheers,
Marissa

--
Marissa Cole
Head of People Analytics & Planning
Redwood Inference
